q: Should I choose one-to-one coaching or a group course?
a: A group course is the most cost-effective way to follow a full structure and routine. One-to-one is fully personalised, with faster feedback and more targeted pacing.

q: What language are lessons taught in?
a: Mainly Cantonese or Mandarin, so the understanding is genuine. Exam execution is always trained in English: questions, key terms and written solutions in markscheme style. Full English delivery is available on request.

Live on Zoom and highly interactive: the core concept first, then targeted past-paper questions with markscheme-focused thinking. After each lesson you get structured homework to consolidate the skill and remove recurring errors. Face-to-face lessons are also available at the centre in Times Square, Causeway Bay.

q: How many hours a week does an IBDP 6 or 7 take?
a: As a baseline, a 6 usually takes around 6 hours a week in total, lessons plus independent practice, and a 7 usually takes 7 or more. The exact plan depends on your current level, how quickly you need to improve and how consistently you can follow the weekly workload.

q: What if my foundation is weak, or I’m behind?
a: That’s very common. We start with a diagnostic to pinpoint the gaps, rebuild the fundamentals topic by topic, and only then scale into past papers and markscheme execution, with a weekly plan that turns weak areas into reliable marks.

For one-to-one coaching, yes: a trial session is available on request, mainly to confirm fit and set expectations. The group courses are complete programmes, from diagnosis through practice and feedback, so a single session wouldn’t show the real process.

q: What should I prepare before the first lesson?
a: An iPad, Apple Pencil and GoodNotes are ideal for clean, fast, interactive work, along with a stable internet connection. Most importantly, be ready to follow the weekly practice plan between lessons; that’s where the biggest gains come from.
